target_customer: Indian expats in the US (NRIs) who need Indian bank accounts, remittances and investing access
problem: NRIs find it slow and paperwork heavy to open NRE and NRO accounts and move money to India. Emigre offered account opening in about 15 minutes plus remittances, bill payment and debit cards.
business_model: Fintech services layered on partner banks; fees and revenue model not stated
product_category: Cross border consumer banking for NRIs

founders.name: Nishant Aggarwal
prior_employers: Head of Product and Growth roles at unnamed startups
education: Dartmouth College, graduate degree in Engineering Management
Delhi College of Engineering, undergraduate degree in Engineering
previous_startups: Two earlier ventures described as reaching six figure revenues (names not given)
founders.background_notes: He also describes consulting engagements advising financial services firms including American Express and Silicon Valley Bank. Source: YC company page.

competitors.name: Zolve
competitors.what: US neobank and credit for immigrants including Indians arriving in the US

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly integration and compliance work with partner banks and remittance rails, with KYC and cross border rules the hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Bank partnerships and compliance know how could help, but nothing in sources shows exclusive partners. Remittance incumbents and later well funded entrants served the same customers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later entrants such as Aspora, formerly Vance and also in YC W22, raised large rounds for the NRI market per 2025 coverage. Nothing shows incumbents buying or copying Emigre.

market_need_then: Zolve's US$15M raise in February 2021 shows investor appetite for immigrant banking. Specific NRI demand data from 2021 or 2022 was not found.

identity.logo: not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct service copy on the site: open accounts in 15 minutes, with holiday promotions.

branding.community_and_virality: No press about the brand, merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: An uncommon word that is also an old design foundry name and a general term, with no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: YC lists Emigre as Inactive, but no shutdown notice, post mortem or acquisition was found, so the cause is not public. The only funding evidence is a small aggregator reported seed of about 125 thousand dollars in June 2022. Later NRI focused companies such as Aspora raised much larger rounds, so the segment attracted capital while Emigre left no public trail.
notes: The website was still live when fetched, advertising a Holi promotion with a March 14 deadline (year not shown), so it may be stale. The seed round rests on a single aggregator (The Company Check); no press confirmation. One aggregator names Kashish Mittal as CEO, conflicting with the YC page naming Nishant Aggarwal; Mittal is not listed as a founder. Headquarters conflicts (San Francisco, Palo Alto, Sunnyvale). Aspora/Vance is not listed as a competitor because the sources found were dated 2025. YC launch post not found. Exit type is unknown because Inactive status is the only evidence.
